programme.title: Lee Miller: A Life on the Front Line
programme.desc: When Lee Miller returned to New York from Europe in October 1932, newspaper reporters were waiting to greet her as her ship docked. Disembarking in a smart beret and fur-collared coat, she smiled for the journalist from the New York World-Telegram. When he referred to her as `one of the most photographed girls in Manhattan', she retorted, `I'd rather take a picture than be one.' Lee Miller is one of the most remarkable female icons of the 20th century.

programme.title: A303: Highway to the Sun
programme.desc: One of Britain's most notorious roads, the A303 is the one that passes Stonehenge on the way to the beaches of Devon and Cornwall. On the way, it whisks drivers through 5,000 years of remarkable moments in English history, and it's the star of this film made for armchair travellers and history lovers. Writer Tom Fort drives its 92-mile length in a lovingly restored Morris Traveller.

programme.title: A Timewatch Guide
programme.desc: Using 70 years of BBC history archive film, Professor Alice Roberts uncovers how the iconic ancient monument of Stonehenge has been interpreted, argued over and debated by some of Britain's leading historians and archaeologists.
